title: ICMP, Ping and Traceroute: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Is anybody out there? Ping is how you ask. And traceroute follows the trail to show you where things stop.

scenes.heading: The return to sender slip
scenes.narration: Think of the postal service's pink return to sender slip. You didn't ask for it. It simply tells you why a delivery failed. That slip is I C M P. Ping is a letter marked, please reply if you get this. If the host is there, it writes back. Traceroute is cleverer. It sends letters that expire early, one hop at a time. Each router that tosses one back reveals itself.

items.story: Please reply if you get this

scenes.heading: Types to remember
scenes.narration: A few I C M P types show up on the exam. Type eight is the echo request, and type zero is the reply. Type three means destination unreachable. And type eleven means time exceeded, which is what traceroute listens for.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three slip-ups. Ping has no ports, because I C M P sits straight on top of I P. A good ping doesn't mean the web server works. And a failed ping doesn't prove there's no connection, because I C M P may be filtered. Also, Cisco traceroute sends U D P probes by default, not I C M P.

items.right: ICMP sits directly on IP, no ports

items.wrong: Ping works so the app works

items.right: It uses UDP probes by default

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva ping and traceroute lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Ping checks if a host answers, using echo request and reply. Traceroute uses the T T L to reveal every router on the way. And a failed ping doesn't always mean a broken network. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva ping and traceroute lab.

points.t: Failed ping is not proof of failure
